PHASE 2: Independently inspect the continuous video to verify EVERY proposed event ID. 
Basketball rules that constrain valid answers:
- A rebound requires a shot that visibly MISSED and left the ball live. If you did not see the ball fail to go through the net, do not report a rebound.
- After a MADE field goal or a MADE free throw the ball is dead. A player collecting the ball is inbounding it, NOT rebounding. Never report a rebound after a made shot.
- A missed free throw is only reboundable if it was the final attempt of its set.
- Offensive rebound means the rebounder is on the SAME team as the shooter; defensive rebound means the OPPOSING team. Decide by team, not by which end of the floor.
- If neither team clearly controls the ball, report no rebound rather than guessing.
- An assist requires a made field goal. Free throws are never assisted.
- A steal and a turnover are one possession change seen from two sides; report one.
Proposals are fallible hypotheses, not evidence. Follow ball and team possession in order. Confirm only when the defining action/outcome is visible. Correct the label if this SAME action is visibly another rubric event (e.g. free throw rather than field goal). Never replace a proposal with an unrelated event; keep its ID, adjust time by at most 2 seconds. Reject only on visible contradiction. Missing, off-camera, occluded or ambiguous evidence means potential_event, NOT rejected. Unknown point value may use a generic field-goal label. An unclear foul/referee/statistical ruling means potential_event for expert review. Do not add proposals or drop IDs. Explain concrete video evidence, not agreement with proposal.
